newsitem.title: USA: Barney's says court approves DIP financing.
newsitem.headline: Barney's says court approves DIP financing.

text.p: Financially troubled Barney's Inc said Tuesday it received approval from a bankruptcy court for $85 million in debtor-in-possession (DIP) financing.
The luxury retailer, which filed for bankruptcy protection last year, said in a statement that the financing was the first component of a $110 million package.
A syndicate led by Bank Boston NA as adminstrative agent was providing the package, it said.
Barney's said it would attend a hearing set for July 17 in New York for approval of the permanent DIP agreement, which would provide it with the remained of the $110 million.
It said the new financing will expire when its reorganization plan receives approval or August 3, 1998, which ever comes first.
The financing replaces its $100 million credit facility with Chase Manhattan Bank, which is scheduled to expire on August 2, 1997, it added.
Barney's said it had already spent about $72 million of its facility with Chase.
